ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $O$ is on line $AB$, $\angle BOD$ and $\angle COD$ are complementary, and $\angle BOC = n\angle EOC$. If $DO \perp OE$, what is the value of $n$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that, since $\angle BOD$ and $\angle COD$ are complementary,\\
we have $\angle BOD + \angle AOD = 180^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle COD = \angle AOD$,\\
Let $\angle COE = x$,\\
then $\angle BOE = nx - x$,\\
since $OD \perp OE$,\\
it follows that $\angle COD + \angle COE = 90^\circ = \angle AOD + \angle BOE$,\\
thus $\angle COE = \angle BOE$,\\
hence $nx - x = x$,\\
and given $x \ne 0$,\\
we find $n = \boxed{2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, O, B are on the same straight line, O is on AB, ray OA points left, and OB points right. Rays OD, OC, OE are all above line AB; according to the positions in the figure, looking counterclockwise along the upper side from ray OB, one passes through OE, OC, OD in sequence, and then reaches OA. The problem statement gives DO ⟂ OE. Reasoning: Let x = ∠EOC, y = ∠BOE. From the order of the rays in the figure, it is known that ∠BOC = ∠BOE + ∠EOC = y + x. According to the supplementary relationship between ∠BOD and ∠COD in the problem statement, there is ∠BOD + ∠COD = 180°. Also because A, O, B are collinear, OA and OB are opposite rays, so ∠BOD + ∠AOD = 180°. Comparing the two equations, obtain ∠COD = ∠AOD. From DO ⟂ OE, ∠DOE = 90°. Looking at the figure, OC is located between OD and OE, so ∠COD + ∠COE = 90°. On the other hand, OA and OB are opposite rays, and OD and OE are perpendicular, therefore on the other side there is ∠AOD + ∠BOE = 90°. Combining ∠COD = ∠AOD, subtracting the two 90° equations gives ∠COE = ∠BOE, that is, x = y. Therefore ∠BOC = x + y = 2x = 2∠EOC. Also the problem statement has ∠BOC = n∠EOC, and ∠EOC is nonzero, so n = 2.
